question: If $A=\left[\begin{matrix}1&0\\ 2&1\end{matrix}\right],$ $B=\left[\begin{matrix}x&0\\ 1&1\end{matrix}\right]$ and $A=B^{2},$ then x equals
explanation:
**Step 1:** Compute $B^2$: $B^2 = \left[\begin{matrix}x&0\\ 1&1\end{matrix}\right] \left[\begin{matrix}x&0\\ 1&1\end{matrix}\right] = \left[\begin{matrix}x \cdot x + 0 \cdot 1 & x \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 1\\ 1 \cdot x + 1 \cdot 1 & 1 \cdot 0 + 1 \cdot 1\end{matrix}\right] = \left[\begin{matrix}x^2&0\\ x+1&1\end{matrix}\right]$.
**Step 2:** Equate $A$ and $B^2$: $\left[\begin{matrix}1&0\\ 2&1\end{matrix}\right] = \left[\begin{matrix}x^2&0\\ x+1&1\end{matrix}\right]$. Comparing matching elements gives $x^2 = 1$ and $x + 1 = 2$, which uniquely yields $x = 1$.
